Apple___Apple_scab.description: A fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis. Dark, scabby lesions appear on leaves and fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply fungicides like Captan or Mancozeb. Remove and destroy infected leaves. Ensure good air circulation.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Avoid overhead watering. Apply preventive fungicide sprays in spring.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa. Causes fruit rot, leaf spots, and branch cankers.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Remove mummified fruits and dead wood. Apply copper-based fungicides. Prune infected branches.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Maintain tree health. Remove debris. Apply fungicides during growing season.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal disease requiring both apple and cedar/juniper trees to complete its life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply myclobutanil or mancozeb fungicides. Remove nearby cedar/juniper trees if possible.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties. Apply preventive fungicide in spring.

Apple___healthy.description: The apple plant appears healthy with no signs of disease.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Continue regular monitoring, proper watering, and fertilization.

Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Maintain acidic soil (pH 4.5–5.5), regular pruning, and adequate sunlight.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease that creates a white powdery coating on leaves and shoots.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur-based fungicides or potassium bicarbonate. Remove infected plant parts.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Ensure good air circulation. Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Regular pruning, proper irrigation, and annual fertilization.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A fungal disease causing rectangular gray or tan lesions on corn leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply fungicides like azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin. Rotate crops.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Use resistant hybrids. Rotate crops. Till soil to bury residue.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Caused by fungus Puccinia sorghi. Creates small, circular to elongate, golden-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Apply fungicides early in disease development. Use resistant corn hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Monitor fields regularly during growing season.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A fungal disease causing long, cigar-shaped tan lesions on corn leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides. Remove and destroy infected crop debris.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Use resistant hybrids. Rotate crops. Manage crop residue.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain proper spacing, adequate nutrients, and regular irrigation.

Grape___Black_rot.description: A serious fungal disease that causes brown lesions on leaves and shrivels berries into black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply mancozeb or myclobutanil fungicides. Remove infected berries and leaves.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune for good air circulation. Apply fungicides starting at bud break.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A chronic grapevine disease complex causing leaf scorch, wood streaking, and fruit spotting.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: No cure available. Remove and destroy infected wood. Apply wound protectants after pruning.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid large pruning wounds. Use clean pruning tools. Apply fungicide to wounds.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Causes dark brown spots with yellow halos on grape leaves.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides. Remove infected leaves.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Ensure good air circulation. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Grape___healthy.prevention: Regular pruning, trellising, and seasonal fungicide program.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: One of the most destructive citrus diseases worldwide. Causes yellow shoots, blotchy leaves, and bitter, misshapen fruit.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacteria (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus) spread by psyllid insects
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure. Remove and destroy infected trees. Control psyllid population with insecticides.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material. Control Asian citrus psyllid. Regular monitoring.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Causes water-soaked spots on leaves, fruit, and twigs that turn brown and fall out.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Apply copper sprays in fall and spring.

Peach___healthy.prevention: Annual pruning, thinning fruit, proper fertilization.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Causes water-soaked, irregular lesions on leaves that turn brown with yellow halos.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides. Remove infected plant material.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seeds. Rotate crops. Avoid overhead watering.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: The bell pepper plant appears healthy.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Causes dark brown spots with concentric rings (target board pattern) on older leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb fungicides. Remove infected leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops. Use certified seed potatoes. Apply preventive fungicides.

Potato___Late_blight.description: The disease that caused the Irish Potato Famine. Creates water-soaked dark lesions that spread rapidly in wet weather.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply fungicides with metalaxyl or cymoxanil IMMEDIATELY. Destroy severely infected plants.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Avoid overhead irrigation. Apply preventive fungicides in wet seasons.

Potato___healthy.prevention: Use certified seed potatoes. Proper hilling and irrigation.

Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Annual pruning, proper trellising, good drainage.

Soybean___healthy.prevention: Crop rotation, proper spacing, weed control.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: White powdery fungal growth on upper leaf surfaces. Causes leaves to yellow and die prematurely.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate fungicides. Remove severely infected leaves.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Ensure good air circulation. Avoid overhead watering.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Causes small, dark purple spots on leaf surfaces that enlarge to form irregular blotches.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Apply captan or myclobutanil fungicides. Remove infected leaves.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Avoid overhead watering. Use mulch. Remove old leaves after harvest.

Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Renovation after harvest, proper irrigation, mulching.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Water-soaked, greasy-looking spots on leaves and fruit that turn brown and ragged.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides. Remove infected plant parts.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seed. Crop rotation. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Dark brown target-like spots with yellow halos on older leaves. Starts from bottom of plant.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb. Remove infected lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Mulch soil. Water at base. Rotate crops annually.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Large, greasy, irregular dark brown spots on leaves. White mold on underside in humid conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply metalaxyl-based fungicides. Remove infected plants immediately.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead watering. Plant resistant varieties. Apply preventive fungicides.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Pale green or yellow spots on upper leaf surface with olive-green velvety mold underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Improve air circulation. Apply copper or chlorothalonil fungicides.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Reduce humidity in greenhouse. Avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Small, circular spots with dark borders and lighter centers on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or copper fungicides. Remove infected leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch soil. Avoid wetting foliage. Crop rotation.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Tiny mites cause stippled, yellowing leaves. Fine webbing visible on undersides.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Apply miticides or insecticidal soap. Use neem oil. Introduce predatory mites.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Keep plants well-watered. Avoid dusty conditions. Avoid broad-spectrum pesticides.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Brown spots with concentric rings giving a target appearance on leaves, stems, and fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Avoid dense planting. Improve air circulation. Crop rotation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Leaves curl upward and turn yellow. Plants are stunted. Spread by whiteflies.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: No cure for infected plants. Control whitefly population. Remove infected plants.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Control whiteflies. Use reflective mulches.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Causes mottled light and dark green patterns on leaves. Stunted growth.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Virus (ToMV) — spreads through contact, tools, hands
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No cure. Remove infected plants. Disinfect tools.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use virus-free seeds. Wash hands before handling plants. Disinfect tools.

Tomato___healthy.prevention: Regular monitoring, proper staking, consistent watering, balanced fertilization.
